key_insight: Ghost tasking adds auxiliary output tasks so even non-parametrizable linear differential systems can be made effectively parametrizable for Gaussian-process-based learning.
engineering_relevance: This enables physics-informed surrogate modeling and inverse problem solving with fewer output tasks and latent functions, especially when data are scarce.
method: Introduce auxiliary “ghost” tasks to augment the system.
Use these tasks to construct a parametrization compatible with Gaussian Processes.
Provide CAS syntax/procedures for polynomial, rational, and meromorphic coefficient systems.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports three experiments with systematic comparisons, and highlights particularly strong performance in an inverse-problem setting with very little data.
watch_item: The approach depends on correct symbolic parametrization construction, so practical use may require careful computer-algebra setup and may be sensitive to model specification.
paper_title: Ghost tasking for parametrized Gaussian Processes solving linear differential equations
